# Known bugs that GoogleSQL's compliance tests (`just compliance`) found. Each case gives
# BigQuery's answer after `!>`, which the emulator does not give yet: the case passes while the
# emulator answers otherwise. Every one of them is to be fixed; a fix fails its case, which then
# moves to the file of its function, written with `=>`.
#
# Inputs come from UNNEST so that the analyzer cannot fold the expression into a constant, which
# it evaluates correctly.

## NaN compares unequal to everything, itself included

SELECT x = x FROM UNNEST([CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "false"

SELECT x != x FROM UNNEST([CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "true"

SELECT x >= 0 FROM UNNEST([CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "false"

SELECT x > CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64) FROM UNNEST([CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "false"

## LIKE escapes with a backslash

SELECT x LIKE 'ab\\%' FROM UNNEST(['ab\\xx']) AS x
!> "false"

SELECT x LIKE 'ab\\_' FROM UNNEST(['ab\\_']) AS x
!> "false"

SELECT x LIKE 'a\\\\%c' FROM UNNEST(['a\\c']) AS x
!> "true"

SELECT x LIKE '\\a' FROM UNNEST(['a']) AS x
!> "true"

## Casts from STRING accept only BigQuery's canonical formats

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS DATE) FROM UNNEST(['2009-02-13 ']) AS x
!> null

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS DATE) FROM UNNEST(['998-02-13']) AS x
!> null

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS DATE) FROM UNNEST(['2009/02/13']) AS x
!> null

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS TIME) FROM UNNEST(['12:34:56.123456+08:00']) AS x
!> null

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS DATETIME) FROM UNNEST([' 2006-01-02 12:34:56.123456 ']) AS x
!> null

SELECT SAFE_CAST(x AS TIMESTAMP) FROM UNNEST(['10000-01-01 00:00:00']) AS x
!> null

## Casts to STRING format as BigQuery does

SELECT CAST(x AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([CAST(0 AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "0"

SELECT CAST(x AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([CAST(123 AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
!> "123"

SELECT CAST(x AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([TIME '01:02:03.12345']) AS x
!> "01:02:03.123450"
